meta.title: "Yes or no?" — how children get herded into someone else's answer frame | Sila Slova
meta.description: Teach your child to refuse forced "yes/no" answers when the truth is more complex. Game-based course for children aged 10–16.

hero.headline: Is your child forced to answer "yes or no" when reality is more complex?
hero.subheadline: "Just answer", "don't dodge", "keep it short". Your child sees there's nuance in the question — but gets pushed to pick one option that doesn't quite fit.

media.alt: A child being pushed into a yes-or-no answer

pain.title: The frame trap: when a choice gets reduced to two options someone else picked for you
pain.body:
"Did you like it or not?" — they both liked it and didn't, and there's a third thing. "Are you for or against?" — they want to ask what exactly. "Yes or no, don't stall" — and your child picks the fast answer because the pressure is on. They feel they didn't say quite what they meant — but no other option was on the table.

This isn't about a child "not being able to answer clearly". It's about control: their field of moves gets narrowed to two, and both options suit the asker. By agreeing to play "yes/no", your child accepts someone else's rules. Anything that doesn't fit that choice — conditions, context, "on one hand, on the other" — gets cut out. And the asker now has an answer they can do whatever they want with.

The result — the child's position gets simplified or rewritten. "But you said yes yourself" — and they meant "yes, but…". That "but" no longer exists in the conversation.

solution.body: 50 episodes, 13 critical thinking lessons. Your child plays — but is actually learning to defend their thinking from someone else's frames.

faq.q: Is it a game or a learning course?
faq.a: Both at the same time. "Sila Slova" looks like a detective series, but every episode contains a hidden critical thinking lesson.

faq.q: What age is it suitable for?
faq.a: Ideal for 10–16 year olds. At this age, children are receptive to new thinking patterns and are still forming their views.

faq.q: How much time is needed each day?
faq.a: 15–20 minutes per episode. Flexible schedule — your child can come back at any convenient time.

faq.q: Is registration required for the demo?
faq.a: No. The demo episode is fully open — no registration, no subscription, no personal data required.
